Cited in the Divine Council Index entry on Deuteronomy 32:8-9.

8: The traditional Hebrew text reads “sons of Israel.” A Hebrew copy from Qumran (4QDeut j) reads “sons of God,” and the Greek Septuagint reads “angels of God.”
Which reading is older decides whether the nations were divided by a future headcount or handed to members of the divine council.

aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abarim.title: Abarim
abarim.note: A range of mountains east of the Dead Sea, looking across at Jericho. Mount Nebo is the peak in it that people know, because that is where Moses stood to see the land he was not going to enter. Israel camped here at the end of the wilderness years.

abib.title: Abib
abib.note: It is the first month of the religious year, and it carries the exodus and Passover. After the exile people called it Nisan.

abiram.title: Abiram
abiram.about: Aaron's adversary living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiram.note: He and Dathan went in with Korah against Moses and Aaron. The ground opened and took him, his household and the rest of them down alive.

abraham.title: Abraham
abraham.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
abraham.note: God called him out of Ur and he went at seventy-five, which is most of what you need to know about him. The nation came out of that.

admah.title: Admah
admah.note: One of the five cities of the plain, always paired with Zeboiim, and destroyed along with Sodom and Gomorrah.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

ar.title: Ar
ar.note: The chief city of Moab on the Arnon, so central that "Ar of Moab" could stand for Moab itself. God told Israel to leave it alone on the way through. Its ruins survive at Rabba in modern Jordan.

aram-naharaim.title: Aram-naharaim
aram-naharaim.note: Aram of the two rivers, upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's relatives settled there, and the wives of Isaac and Jacob came from it.

argob.title: Argob
argob.note: A region of Bashan known for its sixty fortified cities, taken when Israel beat King Og.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer.title: Aroer
aroer.note: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.

ashdoth-pisgah.title: Ashdoth-pisgah
ashdoth-pisgah.note: The slopes of Pisgah, east of the Jordan, in land taken from Sihon the Amorite. It is likely a description of the ridge rather than a place name, the same ridge Moses looked at the promised land from before he died.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

ashtaroth.title: Ashtaroth
ashtaroth.note: Ashtaroth under another spelling, the fortified capital of Og, king of Bashan, east of the Jordan. It went to the half-tribe of Manasseh and then to the Levites of Gershon. The name comes from the goddess Ashtoreth, and the site is generally put at Tell Ashtarah in the Golan.

avims.title: Avims
avims.note: The Avvim lived in villages around Gaza before the Caphtorim, from Crete, drove them out. 2 Kings 17:31 gives the same name to settlers from Avva placed in Samaria by the Assyrians.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal-peor.title: Baal-peor
baal-peor.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal-peor.note: Israel, nearly at the promised land, got drawn into worshipping this Moabite god through Moabite women. A plague followed, and it took Phinehas acting in zeal to stop it.

balaam.title: Balaam
balaam.about: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balaam.note: A prophet, but not an Israelite. Balak of Moab hired him to curse the Israelites. On the way his donkey saw an angel blocking the road that Balaam himself missed, and God made the animal speak to rebuke him.

bashan.title: Bashan
bashan.note: The fertile tableland east of the Jordan, between Gilead and Mount Hermon. Og ruled it, the last of the Rephaim, until Israel beat him and gave the land to half the tribe of Manasseh.

beeroth-of-the-children-of-jaakan.title: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan
beeroth-of-the-children-of-jaakan.note: Wells of the Bene-jaakan, a wilderness camp. From here, in Deuteronomy's itinerary, Israel moved on to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

beor.title: Beor
beor.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
beor.note: Balaam's father, named whenever Balaam is called son of Beor.

bethpeor.title: Bethpeor
bethpeor.note: Across the Jordan from Jericho, in Reuben's land. The sanctuary of Baal-peor nearby gave it its name. Moses gave his final address to Israel in the valley there.

bezer.title: Bezer
bezer.note: A city of refuge for Reuben, east of the Jordan. Anyone who killed a person by accident could run there for protection. It was one of three such cities on that side of the river.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

caphtor.title: Caphtor
caphtor.note: Where the Philistines came from before they settled on Canaan's coastal plain, generally taken to be Crete or somewhere near it in the Aegean.

chinnereth.title: Chinnereth
chinnereth.note: Before anyone called it Gennesaret or Tiberias, the lake was the Sea of Chinnereth, named for a fortified Canaanite city on its northwest shore. The town fell inside Naphtali's land. Under the plural Chinneroth it named the whole district, which Ben-hadad of Syria raided in Baasha's reign.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

dathan.title: Dathan
dathan.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
dathan.note: He and Abiram joined Korah against Moses, and the ground opened under their tents and took them and their families.

dizahab.title: Dizahab
dizahab.note: Place of gold, in the wilderness near where Moses gave his last addresses. Often identified with Dahab on the east coast of Sinai, which keeps the old name, though it cannot be proven.

ebal.title: Ebal
ebal.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
ebal.note: The mountain of the curses, opposite Mount Gerizim near Shechem. Moses ordered six tribes onto Ebal to speak the covenant's curses while six on Gerizim spoke its blessings, and Joshua built an altar there and wrote the law on stones. A Horite chief descended from Seir carried the name too.

edomite.title: Edomite
edomite.note: Esau's descendants, living in Seir south and east of the Dead Sea. Kin to Israel and at odds with it for most of the record. Egyptian texts mention Edom as early as the thirteenth century BC, and its capital Busayra and the copper works at Khirbat en Nahas have both been excavated.

edrei.title: Edrei
edrei.note: Israel met Og, king of Bashan, here, and his whole kingdom fell in that one battle.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

elath.title: Elath
elath.note: A port on the Gulf of Aqaba near Ezion-geber. Solomon held it, Edom took it back, Uzziah recovered it for Judah, and Syria finally got it. Modern Eilat keeps the name.

eleazar.title: Eleazar
eleazar.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eleazar.note: Aaron's third son. Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, and Eleazar became high priest after his father. He worked with Moses on the second census and with Joshua on dividing the land, and his line held the high priesthood for most of the history after.

eliab-3.title: Eliab
eliab-3.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eliab-3.note: His sons were in the wilderness rebellion of Numbers 16 and went down when the ground opened. Deuteronomy 11:6 recalls them by naming him.

emims.title: Emims
emims.note: A people of unusual height who lived in Moab's land before they were pushed out, remembered in Deuteronomy alongside the Anakim.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

esau.title: Esau
esau.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
esau.note: Isaac and Rebekah's elder twin, born red and hairy just ahead of Jacob. He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew, and Jacob later tricked him out of the blessing too, and only after years apart did the two make up in tears. His descendants were the Edomites.

eshcol.title: Eshcol
eshcol.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
eshcol.note: An Amorite ally who helped Abraham get Lot back from Chedorlaomer. The Valley of Eshcol near Hebron, probably named for him or his clan, is where the twelve spies cut the huge cluster of grapes.

euphrates.title: Euphrates
euphrates.note: The great river. It rises in the Armenian highlands and runs some seventeen hundred miles to the Persian Gulf. Genesis has it as one of Eden's four rivers, the promise to Abraham reaches to it, and later Assyria and Babylon came from beyond it.

ezion-geber.title: Ezion-geber
ezion-geber.note: Solomon built his fleet here, at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba near Elath, to sail for Ophir, and Jehoshaphat's ships were wrecked here later. Nelson Glueck dug Tell el-Kheleifeh in the 1930s and called it the site, though later work on the pottery has kept the question open.

gad.title: Gad
gad.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
gad.note: Jacob's seventh son, born to Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe asked for good pasture east of the Jordan and got it. The condition was that Gad's fighting men still crossed over and helped the other tribes take their land first.

gerizim.title: Gerizim
gerizim.note: Opposite Mount Ebal, near Shechem. Six tribes stood on Gerizim to speak the blessings while six on Ebal spoke the curses, as Moses had ordered and Joshua carried out. The Samaritans later built a temple on top as a rival to Jerusalem, which is what the Samaritan woman is asking Jesus about in John 4:20.

geshuri.title: Geshuri
geshuri.note: David married Maacah, daughter of Talmai, the king of Geshur, and so these people were Absalom's family on his mother's side. Their small Aramean kingdom lay east of the Sea of Galilee.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

girgashite.title: Girgashite
girgashite.note: Descended from Canaan in Genesis 10, and one of the peoples on the list Israel was to drive out. Where exactly they lived is unclear, though they are generally placed in the central hill country.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

golan.title: Golan
golan.note: One of the three cities of refuge east of the Jordan, in Bashan, where someone who had killed by accident could run from revenge. It went to the Gershonite Levites and later gave its name to the region, which is why there are Golan Heights today. The exact site is not known.

gomorrah.title: Gomorrah
gomorrah.note: Destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, and the two became shorthand for a people ripe for judgment, from Moses through Jesus and the apostles. No remains have been confirmed. It is generally placed near the southern basin of the Dead Sea.

gudgodah.title: Gudgodah
gudgodah.note: A wilderness stop in Deuteronomy 10:7, just after Moserah where Aaron died. Numbers 33 calls it Hor-haggidgad, and its place in Sinai has not been found.

hazeroth.title: Hazeroth
hazeroth.note: The third camp after Sinai, in the wilderness of Paran. Miriam and Aaron challenged Moses here over his Cushite wife. Miriam was struck with a skin disease and healed when Moses prayed for her.

hermon.title: Hermon
hermon.note: On Israel's northern border, and the snowmelt off it gives the Psalms their picture of dew. It is near Caesarea Philippi, which makes it a likely site for Jesus's transfiguration.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hor.title: Hor
hor.note: Aaron died on Mount Hor, at the edge of Edom near the end of the wandering. His priestly garments were taken off him in sight of the people, and they buried him on the mountain.

horeb.title: Horeb
horeb.note: Another name for Sinai, where Moses met God at the burning bush and Israel received the law, and where Elijah later ran and heard God in a still, small voice after the wind, earthquake and fire.

horims.title: Horims
horims.about: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
horims.note: They lived in the region that became Edom before Esau's descendants pushed them out. Genesis records them as the land's earlier people.

hormah.title: Hormah
hormah.note: Its name means "devoted to destruction", and it was first called Zephath. Israel was beaten there after going into Canaan without the Lord, following the spies' report. Later Israel vowed to destroy the cities of the region, and the vow, kept under Joshua, gave the town its name.

hosea.title: Hosea
hosea.about: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
hosea.note: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, a woman who would be unfaithful, and his taking her back again and again became his book's picture of God with Israel. He prophesied to the north in the decades before it fell to Assyria. The same name, spelled Hoshea, belongs to four other men.

isaac.title: Isaac
isaac.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
isaac.note: Abraham and Sarah's promised son, born when his father was a hundred. God told Abraham to sacrifice him on Mount Moriah and provided a ram at the last moment. Old and blind, he was tricked by Jacob into giving him Esau's blessing, and he never left Canaan or took a second wife.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jabbok.title: Jabbok
jabbok.note: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

jacob.title: Jacob
jacob.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jacob.note: Isaac and Rebekah's younger twin, born holding Esau's heel. He bought his brother's birthright for stew, took his father's blessing by a trick, and ran to his uncle Laban, where he worked fourteen years for Leah and Rachel. On the way home he wrestled all night and came away named Israel. He died in Egypt, near Joseph, and was buried at Machpelah as he had asked.

jair.title: Jair
jair.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jair.note: He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jephunneh.title: Jephunneh
jephunneh.about: Caleb's father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jephunneh.note: Caleb's father, remembered almost entirely as a name in "Caleb son of Jephunneh", which is how the Old Testament tells that Caleb apart from the others.

jericho.title: Jericho
jericho.note: Israel crossed the Jordan and Jericho was the first city it took, walled and gated, with its own king. Achan died for what he stole from the plunder there, a Babylonian robe and silver that belonged to God. By then the place was already ancient: digging at the site has turned up remains about ten thousand years old.

jeshurun.title: Jeshurun
jeshurun.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
jeshurun.note: It is a pet name for Israel, "the upright one", used a few times in Deuteronomy and Isaiah, and usually it comes right before the text shows how far from upright Israel was.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

jotbath.title: Jotbath
jotbath.note: They camped here in the wilderness, between Hor-hagidgad and Ebronah. Moses remembered it as a land of brooks of water, which in that desert stood out. Nobody knows for sure where it was.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kadesh.title: Kadesh
kadesh.note: Kadesh-barnea, Israel's main camp in the wilderness of Zin. Moses sent the twelve spies from there, Miriam died there, and there he struck the rock and lost his way into Canaan. It is usually identified with Ain el-Qudeis or Ain el-Qudeirat, where a fortress of the Israelite period has been dug up.

kadeshbarnea.title: Kadeshbarnea
kadeshbarnea.note: An oasis in the wilderness of Zin, on Canaan's southern edge, where Israel camped for much of the wandering years. The spies went out from here, and the people's fear at their report got that whole generation sentenced to die in the desert. Later it marked the southern boundary of the land.

kedemoth.title: Kedemoth
kedemoth.note: A town in Reuben's land, given to the Merarite Levites. Moses sent messengers from its wilderness to Sihon, king of the Amorites, asking to pass through, and Sihon's refusal led to war.

kibroth-hattaavah.title: Kibroth-hattaavah
kibroth-hattaavah.note: "The graves of craving." The people were sick of manna and demanded meat, and God sent quails in a huge flock. A plague broke out while they ate, and the dead were buried where they fell, so the camp was named for what they had wanted. Moses brought it up again years later when he listed the times they had provoked God.

laban-2.title: Laban
laban-2.note: Named once, in Deuteronomy, and nowhere else.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

levi.title: Levi
levi.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
levi.note: Jacob's third son. He and Simeon massacred the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped, and Jacob cursed them both for it on his deathbed. Even so, Levi's descendants became Israel's priestly tribe, given service at the tabernacle instead of land, partly for their zeal against the golden calf at Sinai.

leviite.title: Leviite
leviite.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
leviite.note: An old spelling of Levite, found in a few manuscripts and translations for the tribe of Levi.

lot.title: Lot
lot.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
lot.note: Abraham's nephew, who came with him from Ur. When their herdsmen started fighting and they split, Lot took the green Jordan valley and ended up living by Sodom. Angels dragged him out before it burned, and his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt. Afterwards his two daughters got him drunk and had sons by him, the fathers of Moab and Ammon.

maachathite.title: Maachathite
maachathite.note: Someone from Maacah, the small Aramean kingdom near Mount Hermon that Israel never fully brought under. Eliphelet, one of David's officers, was a Maachathite.

machir.title: Machir
machir.about: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
machir.note: Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

massah.title: Massah
massah.note: "Testing." Near Rephidim the Israelites ran out of water, quarrelled with Moses and demanded a drink, testing God even as he tested them. The place was also called Meribah, and what happened there became shorthand for a hard heart, used as a warning in Psalm 95 and again in Hebrews 3.

meribah.title: Meribah
meribah.note: "Quarrelling." Israel complained there was no water, and Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it. That cost him the promised land.

meribah-2.title: Meribah
meribah-2.note: The other Meribah, near Rephidim, from Israel's first complaint about water in Exodus 17. Moses' blessing in Deuteronomy and Psalm 95 both name it again.

miriam.title: Miriam
miriam.about: Moses' sister living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
miriam.note: Moses and Aaron's older sister, and a prophetess. She watched over the baby Moses in the reeds of the Nile, and after the crossing of the sea she led Israel's women in song.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moreh.title: Moreh
moreh.note: The oak of Moreh, near Shechem, where Abraham stopped when he first came into Canaan, and Deuteronomy points back to it to show Israel where they would stand.

mosera.title: Mosera
mosera.note: A camp in the wilderness near Mount Hor. Deuteronomy says Aaron died and was buried there, where Numbers puts his death on Mount Hor itself and lists Moseroth nearby, and the two are usually read as the same area.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

nebo.title: Nebo
nebo.note: The mountain in Moab where Moses looked over the promised land before he died, taken as Jebel Neba on the ridge of Pisgah east of the Dead Sea. A Reubenite town nearby had the same name, and the oracles against Moab condemn it.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

og.title: Og
og.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
og.note: King of Bashan and, in Deuteronomy, the last of the Rephaim, with a bed over thirteen feet long. Israel beat him and took his whole kingdom.

paran.title: Paran
paran.note: Ishmael grew up in this wilderness after Hagar was sent away with him, and Israel camped there for part of the long march.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

pethor.title: Pethor
pethor.note: Balaam's hometown, by the Euphrates in northern Mesopotamia. Balak of Moab sent there to hire him. It is generally identified with Pitru.

pharaoh.title: Pharaoh
pharaoh.note: The king Moses stood in front of. God sent Moses to him to bring Israel out of Egypt, and he hardened his heart through plague after plague before he let them go.

pisgah.title: Pisgah
pisgah.note: Moses looked out over the promised land from the top of Pisgah before he died. Balak had brought Balaam up the same ridge in Moab to curse Israel's camp. It belongs to the range called Abarim.

rabbah.title: Rabbah
rabbah.note: Capital of Ammon. David's army besieged it, and Uriah died in that siege, put where the fighting was worst on David's orders.

ramoth.title: Ramoth
ramoth.note: Ramoth in Gilead, one of the cities of refuge east of the Jordan. Israel and Aram fought over it again and again. Ahab took his death wound there in disguise, and later Jehu was anointed king in the same place.

red-sea.title: Red Sea
red-sea.note: Between Egypt and Arabia. Israel crossed it on dry ground in the exodus. When the waters came back, the Egyptian army chasing them was destroyed.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

salcah.title: Salcah
salcah.note: The eastern edge of Israelite settlement. Salcah was a city of Bashan, given to the half tribe of Manasseh once Og, king of Bashan, was beaten.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

senir.title: Senir
senir.note: The Amorite name for Mount Hermon. Ezekiel mentions its fir trees, which went into the ships of Tyre.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sinai.title: Sinai
sinai.note: Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

sion-2.title: Sion
sion-2.note: Named once, in Deuteronomy, and nowhere else.

sirion.title: Sirion
sirion.note: What the Sidonians called Mount Hermon. A psalm has Sirion and Lebanon skipping like a young wild ox at the voice of the Lord.

sodom.title: Sodom
sodom.note: Sodom was destroyed by fire from heaven along with Gomorrah, and the rest of Scripture keeps pointing back to it as the picture of judgment. It was one of the cities of the plain near the Dead Sea.

syrian-2.title: Syrian
syrian-2.note: In Genesis the word marks the family in Paddan-aram as Arameans, and Deuteronomy 26:5 uses it once more.

taberah.title: Taberah
taberah.note: The name means burning. Israel complained in the wilderness, fire from the Lord broke out on the edge of the camp, and it died down when Moses prayed.

thummim.title: Thummim
thummim.note: Paired with the Urim in the high priest's breastpiece, and used the same way, to put a question to God.

tophel.title: Tophel
tophel.note: Deuteronomy opens with Moses speaking to Israel near Tophel. It is generally identified with Tafileh, on the edge of the Edomite plateau east of the Dead Sea.

urim.title: Urim
urim.note: The Urim and Thummim sat in the high priest's breastpiece. They were used to put yes-or-no questions to God. How they actually worked, nobody knows.

zamzummim.title: Zamzummim
zamzummim.note: They were a big people and a numerous one, holding the land east of the Jordan before the Ammonites. Moses says the Lord destroyed them so Ammon could settle there, the way he cleared land for Israel. Some think they are the Zuzim of Genesis 14.

zared.title: Zared
zared.note: The Zered valley, the brook Israel crossed near the end of the wandering on the way around Edom and Moab.

zeboiim.title: Zeboiim
zeboiim.note: One of the five cities of the plain, with Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah and Bela, destroyed with Sodom. In Hosea 11:8 God says he cannot make Israel like Admah and Zeboiim.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zin.title: Zin
zin.note: The Wilderness of Zin, where Kadesh lay. Miriam died there, and there Moses struck the rock in anger when he had been told to speak to it.

zoar.title: Zoar
zoar.note: Lot asked that this little town be spared so he could run to it, and it was, while Sodom and Gomorrah burned. It was first called Bela, and it lay where Moab met the Dead Sea plain.
